Revised event participation fees are intended to strengthen the financial foundation for continued investment in coaching and services

TOKYO, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LEIFRAS Co., Ltd. (Nasdaq: LFS) (the "Company" or "Leifras"), a sports and social business company dedicated to youth sports and community engagement, and a leading operator of children's sports schools and school club activity support businesses in Japan, today announced that it is working to enhance the value of coaching and services at its sports schools and strengthen profitability through event participation fee changes that have already been implemented.

By strengthening its financial foundation for continued investment in coaching and support for members, the Company aims to enhance its services to children and achieve sustainable growth.

1. Enhancing the Value of Leifras' Distinctive Sports School Coaching and Services

In addition to teaching sports skills, the Company emphasizes helping children develop non-cognitive skills such as courtesy, cooperation, and independence.

Drawing on its experience in coaching and program operations, the Company plans to introduce new services to improve day-to-day coaching and support for its members. It aims to build sports schools where children enjoy participating and see their own progress, and where parents and guardians see the value of continued participation.

The Company will disclose further details and the expected launch timeline for the new services once preparations are complete.

2. Strengthening the Financial Foundation Through Event Fee Changes Already in Effect

The Company has already increased participation fees for certain events offered to sports school members, with adjustments determined on an event-by-event basis. It seeks to give children opportunities to gain new experiences through these events and to improve the profitability of event operations.

By combining the event fee changes with operating expense management, the Company aims to improve profitability in its existing business and strengthen the financial foundation for continued investment in coaching and services.

The Company will assess the financial effects of the changes based on factors including event attendance, revenue, and operating expenses.

3. Outlook

To support investment in new services while improving profitability, the Company plans to manage implementation and operating costs and consider improvements to its operating and procurement practices.

While maintaining the resources and procedures needed for coaching and safety, the Company will assess the costs and benefits of each initiative with the aim of delivering services reliably and improving operational efficiency.

The impact of the event participation fee changes on revenue and profit will depend on factors including attendance, the events held and how they are run, and operating expenses. The Company will assess the financial impact of investments in new services and future collaboration as those initiatives take shape. This release does not announce any confirmed increases in revenue or profit or any upward revision to the Company's financial forecasts.

The Company will disclose relevant developments as appropriate.

Exploring Collaboration with OLI in Sports and Education

Building on the mutual understanding developed through its prior collaboration with Oriental Land Innovations Co., Ltd. ("OLI"), the Company will work with OLI to explore ways to benefit children through sports and education.

The two companies will evaluate whether new opportunities leveraging Leifras' experience in sports education and sports school operations could form the basis of new businesses.

The Company will announce specific collaborative initiatives when they are ready to be disclosed, following review and agreement by both companies.

About LEIFRAS Co., Ltd.

Headquartered in Tokyo, Leifras is a sports and social business company dedicated to youth sports and community engagement. The Company primarily provides services related to the organization and operations of sports schools and sports events for children. Leifras was recognized as Japan's largest operator of children's sports schools in terms of both membership and number of schools, as well as the leading provider of school club activity support in terms of the number of contracted schools, according to Tokyo Shoko Research as of December 2025. The Company's approach to sports education emphasizes the development of non-cognitive skills, following the teaching principle "acknowledge, praise, encourage, and motivate." Its holistic approach integrates physical and mental development. Building on its experience and expertise in sports education, Leifras also operates a social business that supports school club activities, provides sports therapy for children with developmental disabilities, and offers exercise programs for the elderly. As of June 30, 2026, the Company supported 2,224 club activities at 478 schools.

DONGGUAN, China, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dogness (International) Corporation ("Dogness" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: DOGZ), a developer and manufacturer of a comprehensive line of Dogness-branded, OEM and private-label pet products, announced that it showcased its new AI-powered smart pet feeders, alongside its established pet product portfolio, at the 30th China International Pet Show (CIPS 2026), held from November 12 to 15 in Guangzhou, China. The exhibition underscores the Company's continued advancement of its AI-driven smart pet care strategy and its global distribution. Through its distribution network across 35 countries and regions, Dogness aims to commercialize its AI-powered pet products and capture new growth opportunities in the smart pet care industry.

Extensive Global Distribution Network Supports AI Product Commercialization

Dogness's channel network now covers 35 countries and regions worldwide. It sells through global retailers and specialized pet channels including Walmart, Costco, Petco and Pet Valu, online platforms such as Amazon and Chewy, as well as brand and industry partners like Velcro. This broad network and the Company's long-standing relationships provide a foundation for presenting products, gathering market feedback and exploring new collaborations. They also support Dogness's efforts to introduce its new AI products to different markets and adapt its product portfolio to local needs, strengthening its relationships with major international retailers.

Driving AI Innovation in Smart Pet Care Through a Structured Matrix of AI Products

While strengthening its established pet supplies business, Dogness continues to expand the development and production of AI-enabled pet products. The Company continues to invest in R&D for intelligent functions and products designed for specific pet care needs, pursuing a two-track approach that combines an established product foundation with continued AI innovation.

  • New AI Products: Advancing the AI Strategy through Smart Feeding

At CIPS 2026, Dogness showcased the F01B and F10B AI feeders, allowing attendees to explore smart feeding and scenario-based interaction features through hands-on demonstrations. The 3.6-liter F10B, built with Google Gemini, features a high-definition night-vision camera and AI-powered behavior recognition that alerts owners to unusual activity through the Dogness mobile app. The F01B offers a larger 8-liter capacity in a distinct design. AI feeders are an important entry point within the Company's expanding portfolio of AI pet products. Dogness continues to invest in R&D and refine products around real-world pet care needs, advancing the application of AI capabilities in everyday feeding scenarios.

More importantly, Dogness's AI strategy is not a collection of standalone devices but a scenario-driven product matrix. Its technical strengths are reflected in three areas: first, scenario-based interaction capabilities developed around high-frequency pet care scenarios including feeding, interaction and location tracking; second, integrated hardware-software-scenario design that enables AI features to deliver a seamless user experience throughout real-world usage journeys; and third, sustained R&D and iteration capabilities, underpinned by the Company's continued investment in intelligent function development and scenario-based product pipeline reserves. AI feeders serve as the primary entry point, as the product matrix extends into location-tracking use cases, with AI-enabled water fountains in the pipeline to form a multi-scenario AI product matrix covering feeding, hydration and location tracking.

  • Established Product Portfolio as a Robust Foundation for AI-Driven Growth

At CIPS 2026, Dogness also presented quick-release pet leashes, the slow-recovery R06 retractable leash, paw cleaner cups, training mats and reflective collars, covering everyday walking, cleaning, training and visibility needs.

The established portfolio delivers four key pillars supporting Dogness's AI product development: an established customer base and repeat-purchase relationships that create a natural on-ramp for AI products; brand recognition that lowers market education costs for new AI offerings; an integrated, in-house supply chain covering design and R&D, material sourcing, manufacturing and quality control, which supports production of AI products with consistent quality and effective cost control; and existing sales channels, including distributor networks, retail outlets and e-commerce operations, to support the distribution and promotion of AI products.

Furthermore, Dogness's traditional and AI businesses unlock opportunities for cross-selling and mutual promotion. Channel credibility and user relationships built through its established product lineup help AI products gain market traction. In turn, AI products elevate the brand's technological positioning and customer value, reinforcing the established product portfolio. As such, Dogness has built a growth framework wherein its established product portfolio stabilizes the core business and its structured AI product matrix is intended to drive incremental growth.

Silong Chen, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Dogness, commented: "CIPS 2026 enables us to leverage our well-established worldwide sales network and customer base, supported by end-to-end R&D and manufacturing systems, to further advance our strategic transformation from a traditional global pet products manufacturer into a global AI-powered smart pet care technology company, and accelerate the global commercialization of AI-powered pet products."

Dogness (International) Corporation was founded in 2003 from the belief that dogs and cats are important, well-loved family members. Through its smart products, hygiene products, health and wellness products, and leash products, Dogness' technology simplifies pet lifestyles and enhances the relationship between pets and pet caregivers. The Company ensures industry-leading quality through its fully integrated vertical supply chain and world-class research and development capabilities, which have resulted in over 200 patents and patents pending. TORONTO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Generation Mining Limited (TSX: GENM) (OTCǪB: GENMF) (“Gen Mining” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce that, further to its news release dated September 14, 2026, it has completed a non-brokered private placement (the “Offering”) of unsecured, subordinated convertible notes of the Company (the “Convertible Notes”) with Canada Growth Fund Inc. (“CGF”) and Canada Infrastructure Bank (“CIB”, and together with CGF, the “Noteholders”) for aggregate gross proceeds of $100 million, pursuant to which each Noteholder subscribed for $50 million of Convertible Notes.

The financing will help advance construction of the Marathon Project and support the development of a new domestic supply of copper and palladium in Northwestern Ontario.

“We sincerely appreciate the support of Canada Growth Fund and the Canada Infrastructure Bank,” said Jamie Levy, President and Chief Executive Officer of Gen Mining. “CGF and the CIB have been invaluable partners in our mission to build Canada’s next critical minerals mine. Their commitment to the Marathon Project reflects a shared focus on securing a domestic supply of copper and palladium for Canada.”

The Convertible Notes, the issuance of which was approved at a special meeting of shareholders of the Company held on November 26, 2026, are convertible into an aggregate of up to 111,111,111 Common Shares at an initial conversion price of $0.90 per Common Share, subject to anti-dilution adjustments for any share splits, consolidations, reclassifications and dividends paid in Common Shares. The Convertible Notes will bear interest at a rate of 9.0% per annum. Interest will be calculated and payable in cash semi-annually in arrears, to the extent that the distribution conditions under the senior secured project finance facility of the Company (the “Senior Facilities”), once in place following settlement and execution of final documentation, do not restrict such cash payment. The Convertible Notes will mature on the earlier of: (i) November 27, 2037; or (ii) if the Senior Facilities and the subordinated debt facility of $200 million with CIB (the “CIB Facility”) have been repaid in full, including through refinancing, then on the later of: (A) November 27, 2033; and (B) 12 months after the repayment of the Senior Facilities and the CIB Facility.

Additional shares may be issuable upon conversion of payment-in-kind interest. For additional information about the Convertible Notes, please refer to the Company’s management information circular dated October 19, 2026, available under the Company’s issuer profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

The proceeds from the Offering will be used by the Company to fund the development, construction and operation of the Company’s 100%-owned Marathon Copper-Palladium Project (the “Marathon Project”), together with associated general and administrative and financing costs.

The Offering remains subject to final approval of the Toronto Stock Exchange (“TSX”).

Immediately prior to the Offering, CGF had ownership and control over 138,950,000 Common Shares, representing approximately 19.8% of the issued and outstanding Common Shares on a non-diluted basis. The Convertible Notes are subject to a blocker feature, which prohibits the issuance of Common Shares upon the conversion of the Convertible Notes where such issuance would result in CGF, together with its affiliates, holding more than 19.9% of the issued and outstanding Common Shares. Conversion of the Convertible Notes in excess of the 19.9% threshold will be cash settled by the Company.

CGF acquired the Convertible Notes for investment purposes and not with a view to materially affecting control of the Company. Depending upon market conditions and other factors, including pursuant to certain rights granted to CGF under the investor rights agreement dated as of September 21, 2026, entered into between CGF and the Company, CGF may, from time to time, acquire or dispose of additional securities of the Company, in the open market, by private agreement or otherwise, or acquire interests in or enter into related financial instruments involving a security of the Company.

A copy of CGF’s early warning report with respect to the Offering will be filed on SEDAR+ ( www.sedarplus.ca ) promptly, and, in any event, within two business days from the date hereof. CGF has a registered office located at 79 Wellington Street West, Suite 3000, Toronto, Ontario, M5K 1N2.

Generation Mining Limited (TSX: GENM | OTCǪB: GENMF) is a Canadian critical minerals development company focused on building the Marathon Copper-Palladium Project in Northwestern Ontario. The Marathon Project is expected to be a long-life, low-cost mining operation producing critical minerals essential to electrification, clean energy technologies and emissions reduction. As of November 25, 2026, FFAI beneficially owned approximately 14.7 million shares of FFR common stock, representing approximately 53% of FFR's 27.7 million shares currently outstanding. All newly issued FFR shares received by FFAI in the transaction are subject to an 18‑month lock-up period. Based on FFR's closing market price on November 25, 2026, the implied value of FFAI's expected ownership position would be approximately $41 million.

"FFAI's substantial ownership position reflects its continuing strategic alignment with FFR," said YT Jia, Global CEO of FFAI and FFR. KeyBank shares warning signs and practical steps for avoiding phishing, fake shopping sites, payment app scams and other holiday fraud

CLEVELAND, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As holiday shopping picks up, so do opportunities for scammers.

Consumers shopping online, tracking packages, buying gift cards or donating to charities can encounter increasingly convincing fraud attempts. Scammers are also using artificial intelligence to create fake retail websites, emails, text messages and even AI-generated voices designed to impersonate trusted companies or people.

Knowing what to look for can help consumers recognize potential fraud before they share personal information or send money.

What are the most common holiday shopping scams?

Here are several scams consumers should watch for during the holiday season:

Bank imposter scams. Fraudsters may call, text or email pretending to represent a consumer's bank. They may claim there has been a suspicious transaction or login attempt, then ask for a one-time passcode, login credentials or debit card information. KeyBank will not initiate a call or text asking for your online banking username or password. KeyBank also will not ask a client to send money to themselves using Zelle®, an account transfer or a wire payment, or request remote access to your computer or mobile device. However, in some cases, we will call to verify your identity by asking for a one-time passcode that is sent to your mobile device.

Phishing and smishing scams. Fraudulent emails and text messages can look like legitimate communications from retailers, banks or delivery companies. Scammers may also use AI to create convincing fake retail websites and communications intended to capture debit card, credit card or other personal information. A common example is a fake package-delivery message asking for payment to release or redeliver an order.

Vishing and AI voice scams. Criminals can use AI-generated voices in phone calls to impersonate customer service representatives, delivery companies, family members or others in an effort to obtain sensitive information.

Payment app scams. Consumers should be cautious when an unfamiliar seller asks for payment through Zelle®, Venmo, Cash App, wire transfer or cryptocurrency. Recovering money sent to a fraudulent seller through these methods can be difficult.

Online marketplace scams. Fraudsters may advertise popular holiday gifts at unusually low prices, then request advance payment through a payment app, gift card or cryptocurrency before disappearing.

Gift card scams. Criminals may tamper with gift cards displayed on retail racks or convince victims to provide gift card numbers over the phone to make supposedly urgent payments.

Charity scams. The season of giving can also attract criminals impersonating legitimate charities or disaster-relief organizations through phone calls, texts, emails and social media.

5 ways to shop more safely this holiday season

A few habits can make it harder for scammers to succeed:

  1. Be skeptical of unexpected communications. Don't automatically trust an unsolicited call, email or text, even if it appears legitimate. Avoid clicking unfamiliar links or attachments and independently verify the communication using a known phone number, website or app.
  2. Monitor financial accounts regularly. Reviewing account activity frequently can help consumers identify unauthorized transactions sooner. KeyBank recommends clients check their accounts daily and report unauthorized activity immediately.
  3. Turn on multi-factor authentication. MFA provides another layer of account security by requiring an additional form of verification when signing in.
  4. Use secure internet connections. Avoid conducting financial transactions over public Wi-Fi. A secure Wi-Fi connection or virtual private network, or VPN, can help protect data.
  5. Look for buyer protection. When shopping through online marketplaces, consider platforms offering buyer protections and avoid paying sellers who cannot be independently verified.

Holiday scam warning signs consumers shouldn't ignore

Consumers should pause when they encounter:

  • A deal that seems too good to be true
  • An unexpected call, email or text
  • Pressure to send money or act immediately
  • Requests to keep a transaction secret
  • Requests for passwords, codes or sensitive financial information
  • Demands for payment through gift cards, cryptocurrency or payment apps
  • Last-minute requests to change payment information
  • Requests for remote access to a computer or device

These behaviors can indicate an attempted scam.

CHARLOTTE, NC, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Greenland Mines Ltd (Nasdaq: GRML; FSE: HK6) (“Greenland Mines” or the “Company”) today announced that President Bo Møller Stensgaard has accepted an invitation to join the “Building Nordic Value Chains” panel discussion at the Nordic Forum on Raw Materials (“RAW”) conference, “Strengthening Collaboration on Critical and Strategic Raw Materials,” in Nuuk, Greenland, December 8–10, 2026. Dr. Stensgaard and Robert Møller, the Company’s Nuuk-based Permitting & Community Officer, plan to attend the conference.

Convened through personal invitations, the conference will bring together a selected group of senior representatives and experts from industry, academia, research organisations, public authorities and governments across the Nordic region. Organizers have identified participants based on their experience, expertise, and ability to contribute to a strategic dialogue on the future of Nordic critical and strategic raw-material cooperation.

Greenland Mines views the invitation to contribute to the panel as recognition of the practical perspective it brings through its active development projects, Greenlandic presence, and relationships across the Nordic minerals sector.

Connecting Greenlandic Resources with Nordic Industrial Strength

The conference will examine how closer Nordic cooperation can support research, innovation, investment, skills, and competitive mineral-based value chains. RAW is coordinated by Nordic mining and minerals industry associations and supported by Nordic Innovation, an organization within the Nordic Council of Ministers. Its network connects industry, research, finance, and public-sector stakeholders across the Nordic countries and autonomous regions.

Through the panel discussion, Greenland Mines intends to contribute experience from advancing the Sarfartoq neodymium-praseodymium rare earth project in southwest Greenland and the Skaergaard palladium-platinum-gold project in southeast Greenland. Its focus will be on connecting Greenlandic resources with Nordic expertise and industrial capacity, and on the practical requirements for moving projects forward: technical studies, permitting, environmental understanding, infrastructure, financing, and meaningful local participation.

“The Nordic region has the resources, technical expertise and industrial capabilities to make a much greater contribution to critical-mineral supply security. The challenge is to connect those strengths and translate them into responsible projects and competitive supply chains,” said Bo Møller Stensgaard, President of Greenland Mines.

“The invitation to join the ‘Building Nordic Value Chains’ panel gives us an opportunity to bring a Greenland-focused developer’s perspective to this strategic discussion,” Stensgaard continued. “Our focus is what it takes to move from geological potential and resource development to technically sound, financeable and permitted mining projects - and where Nordic cooperation can make a practical difference.”

Grounded in Greenland, Connected Across the North Atlantic

The Company’s delegation combines project-development leadership with a local perspective. Robert Møller, who is Greenlandic/Inuit and based in Nuuk, brings local knowledge and a focus on permitting and community engagement to the Company’s participation.

Alongside the conference, Greenland Mines is arranging separate meetings in Nuuk with local institutional stakeholders, authorities, and international representatives in Nuuk to discuss the Company’s activities, responsible project development and opportunities for local value creation, and to provide updates on its ongoing international partnership activities.

“Our presence in Nuuk is about more than participating in a conference,” Stensgaard continued. “It is an opportunity to listen, strengthen relationships and discuss how our projects can progress responsibly and create lasting value in Greenland. With Robert based in Nuuk, we bring an ongoing local presence to that dialogue. International expertise and investment must connect with Greenlandic priorities, local communities, businesses and opportunities for people in Greenland.”

The conference’s emphasis on cross-border cooperation aligns with Greenland Mines’ North Atlantic Critical Metals Corridor vision: connecting responsibly developed Greenlandic resources with Nordic and wider allied capabilities in research, technology, logistics, processing, investment and industrial markets.

Sarfartoq and Skaergaard provide complementary foundations for that vision, spanning rare earth magnet materials and palladium, platinum and gold. The Company sees Nordic collaboration as an opportunity to strengthen the technical and commercial relationships needed to advance these projects while supporting potential economic activity in Greenland and the wider North Atlantic.

“Supply security will not be built through isolated projects or policy announcements alone,” Dr. Stensgaard added. “It requires resources, infrastructure, technology, capital and local participation to move together. That is the practical cooperation we want to help build - and why this dialogue in Nuuk matters.”

Participation in the conference, panel discussion and separate stakeholder meetings does not constitute endorsement of Greenland Mines by the organisers, meeting counterparties or participating institutions and does not imply any financing, permitting, commercial agreement or partnership commitment.

Greenland Mines Ltd is listed on Nasdaq and develops mineral assets in Greenland, including the Skaergaard precious-metals project in southeast Greenland and the Sarfartoq neodymium-praseodymium rare earths project in southwest Greenland. Its North Atlantic Critical Metals Corridor strategy seeks to connect Greenland resources with processing capacity and industrial customers in the United States and allied countries.   • Tiziana reports favorable safety and tolerability profile with intranasal foralumab after 48.1 patient-years cumulative exposure
  • Intranasal foralumab has been well tolerated across all studies, with no serious adverse events related to study drug

BOSTON, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tiziana Life Sciences, Ltd. (Nasdaq: TLSA) (“Tiziana” or the “Company”), a biotechnology company developing breakthrough immunomodulation therapies with its lead development candidate, intranasal foralumab, a fully human anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody, today announced the submission of its annual Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This DSUR (dated September 2, 2024 to September 30, 2026) reports no drug-related serious adverse events after a cumulative exposure of 48.1 patient-years, highlighting the safety and tolerability data profile of intranasal foralumab in treating neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases, including non-active secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (na-SPMS), Alzheimer’s disease (AD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

“We have seen 48.1 patient-years of cumulative foralumab exposure with no study drug-related serious adverse events, a milestone that reinforces the safety of our intranasal approach,” said Ivor Elrifi, Chief Executive Officer of Tiziana. “Acceptable safety and tolerability continue to be observed across our CNS programs, supporting continued clinical development. We believe that this favorable safety and tolerability profile additionally paves the way for exploring the use of nasal foralumab, not only as a mono-therapy, but also as a multiple sclerosis combination therapy for patients on anti-CD20 approved therapies such as Ocrevus® (ocrelizumab). We have previously announced a memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed with King Abdullah International Medical Research Center (KAIMRC) in Saudi Arabia, with our intention to collaborate on a clinical trial evaluating this combination therapy.”

Key highlights from the submission include:

  • Expanded Access Program (IND 161148): As of 30 September 2026, fourteen (14) patients with na-SPMS were treated with nasal foralumab at Brigham and Women’s Hospital. They received nasal foralumab at 50 or 100 micrograms per dosing day (6 days per three-week cycle) for durations ranging from 23 weeks to 4.7 years. The total cumulative patient exposure in this study is 32.1 patient-years.

  • TILS-021 Randomized Trial and TILS-022 Open-Label Extension: This randomized, double-blind trial in patients with na-SPMS administers foralumab intranasally at doses of either 50 or 100 µg in addition to placebo. The trial completed enrollment (48 patients total) in the summer of 2026, with the last patient dosed on 17 August 2026. Thirty (30) patients were administered foralumab. The total estimated cumulative patient exposure in this study and the open-label extension is 10.25 patient-years.

  • Alzheimer’s Disease (TILS-024 and Expanded Access): Tiziana initiated study TILS-024 in Q4 2025. This randomized, controlled, double-blind study uses a 3:1 treatment ratio (50 µg intranasal foralumab versus placebo) with the same dosing schedule. It is estimated that eleven (11) patients have received nasal foralumab in the reporting period, with an estimated cumulative patient exposure of 1.4 years. One (1) patient with moderate AD continued treatment in a single-patient expanded access IND (IND 172400) at 50 micrograms intranasally per dosing day (6 days per three-week cycle) and has completed 93 weeks of therapy (1.8 total patient-years).

  • Multiple System Atrophy (TILS-025): Initiated in the second half of 2025, this open-label study uses the same dosing schedule. Seven (7) patients have received nasal foralumab for 3–8 weeks duration, with a cumulative patient exposure of 2.50 years.

  • ALS (TILS-ALS-01): Initiated in Q3 2026, this randomized, controlled, double-blind study uses a 3:1 treatment ratio (50 µg intranasal foralumab versus placebo) with the same dosing schedule. It is estimated that two (2) patients have received nasal foralumab in the reporting period, with an estimated cumulative patient exposure of 0.04 years.

In these studies investigating intranasal foralumab in central nervous system (CNS) diseases, favorable safety and tolerability have been observed. During the reporting period, no new risks were identified that resulted in significant protocol amendments for any of the clinical studies. The types and frequency of reported adverse events are generally consistent with those from previous reporting periods.

In conclusion, no substantive changes to the previous knowledge of foralumab safety and tolerability when administered intranasally to patients with CNS disease were identified during the reporting period. The benefit:risk for intranasal foralumab remains favorable in these patients and continued clinical development in CNS patients is warranted. No new actions to address the safety of intranasally delivered foralumab have arisen from the current reporting period.

The cumulative estimated drug exposure for these subjects is 48.1 patient-years. No serious adverse events so far attributed to study drug in nasal foralumab CNS studies. The safety profile of intranasal foralumab aligns with prior studies of foralumab administered intravenously (IV) in healthy volunteers, patients with Crohn’s disease, and kidney transplant recipients. Unlike IV administration, which has been linked to infusion-related reactions seen with other anti-CD3 monoclonal antibodies, nasal delivery of foralumab appears to have better tolerability, with no such issues observed to date.

About Foralumab
Foralumab, a fully human anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody, is a biological drug candidate that has been shown to stimulate T regulatory cells when dosed intranasally. The recently announced INFORM-MS Phase 2a, placebo controlled, double blind trial met its dual primary endpoints for (1) statistically significant reduction (p=0.0168) in microglial activation as measured by TSPO PET imaging in patients treated with 50 ug nasal foralumab as compared to placebo and (2) safety/tolerability. Foralumab treated subjects showed statistically and clinically significant improvements in Modified Fatigue Impact Scale (MFIS) scores compared with their own baseline scores after only 12 weeks of drug therapy. Subjects treated with 50 ug nasal foralumab saw a -6.17 point decrease from baseline (p=0.035), and those treated with 100 ug experienced a -7.18 decrease from baseline (p=0.040). At present, 14 patients with Non-Active Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis (na-SPMS) have been dosed in an open-label intermediate sized Expanded Access (EA) Program (NCT06802328) with either an improvement or stability of disease seen within 6 months in all patients. Intranasal foralumab is also currently being studied in additional Phase 2 trials in Alzheimer’s disease (AD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Intranasal foralumab is the only fully human anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody (mAb) currently in clinical development. Immunomodulation by intranasal foralumab represents a novel avenue for the treatment of neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative human diseases.[1],[2]

About Tiziana Life Sciences

Tiziana Life Sciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing breakthrough therapies using transformational drug delivery technologies to enable alternative routes of immunotherapy. Tiziana’s innovative intranasal approach has the potential to provide an improvement in efficacy as well as safety and tolerability compared to intravenous (IV) delivery. Tiziana’s lead candidate, intranasal foralumab, which is the only fully human anti-CD3 mAb currently in clinical development, has demonstrated a favorable safety profile and clinical response in patients in studies to date. Tiziana’s technology for alternative routes of immunotherapy has been patented with several applications pending and is expected to allow for broad pipeline applications.

End-to-end encryption, self-destructing messages, encrypted file transfers, Chat-by-Invite, and Sekur ID identity management with no phone number required all remain in place, built on Sekur's proprietary, Swiss-hosted architecture with zero reliance on Big Tech cloud infrastructure.

The new interfaces and December launches are intended to prepare Sekur for 2027. The Company has started pre-sales efforts in the U.S. and internationally, including Africa, Latin America, the Middle East, and Central and Eastern Europe, and plans to enter 2027 with a refreshed, easier-to-use platform and an expanded set of solutions to offer enterprise, government, defense, and executive clients in those markets. Sekur Core Communications Solutions

Sekur delivers secure communications that work within and beyond the Sekur network, operating independently of conventional telecom infrastructure to reduce exposure to interception, SIGINT collection, traffic analysis, metadata exploitation, and hostile surveillance in contested environments. No Sekur solution data-mines or location-tracks its users.

All solutions are built on proprietary architecture with zero reliance on Big Tech cloud infrastructure, meeting the privacy, security, and OPSEC requirements of intelligence agencies, defense and federal organizations, military commands, diplomatic missions, government agencies, executives, and professionals handling CUI and other sensitive, mission-critical information. A fully encrypted communications platform engineered on proprietary HeliX data transfer architecture, purpose-built to defeat telecom network tracing, resist Pegasus-style malware intrusion, and support CUI handling requirements. SekurOne is designed for defense and federal officials, military commanders, government leaders, and executives conducting confidential, operational, or sensitive conversations where standard carrier-based voice and video platforms present unacceptable interception and exploitation risk.

Call-by-Invite capability via SMS or SekurSend email ensures controlled access and eliminates unsolicited contact. Each user is assigned a unique Sekur ID for identity management, with no phone number required - preserving user privacy across all voice and video communications.

An enterprise- and government-grade encrypted email platform designed for defense and federal agencies, military commands, senior government officials, C-suite executives, and organizations handling confidential and operationally sensitive communications, including CUI correspondence. Built on proprietary architecture with zero dependence on Big Tech cloud infrastructure and no metadata tracking, SekurMail keeps sensitive communications private between sender and recipient.

Key capabilities include SekurSend/SekurReply for secure delivery to non-Sekur recipients without exposing sender identity or message content; full message delivery control and audit capability; encrypted file transfer; custom domain support for organizational integration; and active protection against phishing, social engineering, and Business Email Compromise (BEC) attacks targeting corporate and administrative networks.

SekurMessenger - Secure Team Messaging and Collaboration

A secure messaging platform providing end-to-end encrypted text, file transfer, voice messages, and collaboration capabilities for defense, military, government, and executive teams coordinating operational and mission-sensitive information, including CUI material. SekurVPN - Enterprise Network Security and Identity Protection

An enterprise-grade Virtual Private Network leveraging proprietary HeliX encryption technology, engineered to provide secure internet access, identity obfuscation, and traffic protection for defense organizations, military and federal personnel, government agencies, and executives operating across remote, traveling, deployed, forward, or untrusted network environments.

It is built for defense, government, and executive use cases - including protection of traffic associated with CUI and operationally sensitive workflows - where standard commercial VPN solutions present unacceptable privacy and security risk.

SekurRelay - Executive-Level Secure Email Integration

An enterprise-grade secure email relay solution enabling domain splitting, which allows organizations to establish secure communications at the executive, board, or senior staff level without requiring full organizational migration or infrastructure overhaul.

SekurRelay removes one of the most significant barriers to large-scale defense, government, and enterprise deployment, enabling phased adoption that protects command leadership, flag officers, and the highest-value personnel and communications immediately while broader organizational rollout proceeds. The proposed delisting is subject to CSE approval, and the Company will announce the effective date of the delisting once confirmed by the CSE. The Company's common shares are expected to continue to be quoted on the OTCQB Venture Market under the symbol "JSDA."

The voluntary delisting is expected to reduce exchange, exchange related-compliance and administrative costs while maintaining access to the Company's existing U.S. trading market.

The Company continues to actively pursue an uplisting of its common shares to a major U.S. national securities exchange as part of its broader capital markets strategy. Provides Drilling Update on its Flagship Elida Porphyry Cu-Mo-Ag Deposit

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Element 29 Resources Inc. (TSXV: ECU) (OTCQX: EMTRF) (BVL: ECU) ("Element 29" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has signed a three-year surface Access Agreement with the host community at its Flor de Cobre Porphyry Copper-Molybdenum ("Cu-Mo") Project ("Flor de Cobre" or the "Project") in southern Perú (Figure 1). This agreement, which expires November 5, 2029, secures long-term access to Flor de Cobre and marks a significant milestone for the Company.

Richard Osmond, President and CEO, commented: "The successful signing of the community Access Agreement underscores the strength of our local relationships and commitment to advancing our projects in close collaboration with rightsholders. We remain focused on progressing Flor de Cobre in a responsible and mutually beneficial manner as we work to unlock its full exploration potential. We are grateful to the community for their ongoing support and partnership."

The signing of the Access Agreement with the host Indigenous community at Flor de Cobre satisfies the final outstanding community-access requirement associated with the Company's application for a Permiso de Inicio de Actividades ("PIA") drilling permit. The PIA application seeks authorization to commence exploration drilling covered by the already approved Declaración de Impacto Ambiental ("DIA") environmental certificate, which provides for drilling from up to 40 platforms over a five-year period (see the March 1, 2024 news release).

The Company previously received an exemption from the Consulta Previa ("Prior Consultation") process on October 21, 2024 (see October 31, 2024 news release), following a review by the Peruvian Ministry of Energy and Mines ("MINEM") of the Collective Impacts Report and its assessment of the potential impacts of exploration drilling on the host Indigenous community's lands.

The Company submitted the PIA application to MINEM on November 10, 2026, which remains pending review and final approval.

Elida Drilling Program Update

The ongoing Elida drilling program is being conducted under the 40-platform PIA drill permit approved in July of 2026 (see the July 28, 2026, news release). The Company started the year with two diamond drill rigs, then added a third rig in September and a fourth is scheduled to arrive in early December. The Company has completed 9,292 metres of its planned 10,000-metre 2026 program. Cumulative drilling at Elida now totals 32,699 metres, more than twice the 14,361 metres of drilling used to prepare the 2022 initial pit-constrained Inferred Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE") ¹.

Elida is accessible year-round for drilling, and the Company plans to continue the program with four rigs for the remainder of 2026 and through 2027. Local assay laboratory turnaround is currently two to four weeks.

Assay Results Pending for Recently Completed Holes

Recently completed holes ELID044 and ELID045 reached depths of 1,812.8 metres and 1,820.6 metres, respectively. Both holes focused on step-out drilling to extend Zone 1 westward and evaluate potential resource expansion beyond the current MRE. They were designed to follow up on the long-mineralized intercepts in ELID033, ELID035 and ELID037, which suggest the potential for stronger Cu-Mo-Ag mineralization at depth and westward toward the contact with the Coastal Batholith (Figure 2).

ELID044 intersected 1,572.9 metres of potassic-altered volcanosedimentary rocks, from 35.1 metres below the bedrock surface to 1,608.0 metres downhole. The interval contains porphyry-related stockwork veining of varying intensity, with disseminated and stringer chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. At 1,608.0 metres, the hole entered a potassic-altered granodiorite intrusion with stockwork veining and disseminated and stringer chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. The granodiorite continued to the end of the hole at 1,812.8 metres, where drilling was shut down due to the depth limitations of the rig.

ELID045 intersected potassic-altered volcanosedimentary rocks, from 78.7 metres below the bedrock surface to 1,245.5 metres downhole. The interval contains stockwork veining, with disseminated and stringer chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. At 1,245.5 metres, the hole intersected 61.2 metres of potassic-altered granodiorite cut by narrow fingers of potassic-altered quartz monzonite porphyry ("QMP"). Both rock types contain stockwork veining with disseminated chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. From 1,306.7 metres, the hole intersected 358.9 metres of potassic-altered QMP, interpreted as an early-intermineral porphyry, with stockwork veining and disseminated and stringer chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. Below this interval, the hole re-entered potassic-altered, locally brecciated volcanosedimentary rocks, with stockwork veining and disseminated and stringer chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. The hole terminated at 1,820.6 metres due to the depth limitations of the rig.

ELID046 was drilled to a depth of 956.2 metres and was the first hole to evaluate Zone 4, a high-priority target immediately west of Zone 1 within the Elida porphyry cluster. Zone 4 hosts a mineralized porphyry stock emplaced along the contact between the Coastal Batholith and volcanosedimentary rocks. The stock and host rocks exhibit phyllic alteration overprinting earlier potassic alteration, as well as visible copper-oxide staining and anomalous Cu-Mo rock geochemistry. These features support the target's prospectivity for Cu-Mo-Ag mineralization. The hole intersected a 395.9-metre interval of phyllic-overprinted, potassic-altered QMP beginning at 197.8 metres downhole. The QMP is interpreted as a potassic-altered intermineral porphyry intrusion, with stockwork veining containing disseminated and stringer chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. Locally, chalcocite and covellite occur as disseminations and rimming chalcopyrite and pyrite.

True widths are unknown, and assay results for all three holes are pending.

Metallurgical Test Work

In parallel, the Company is advancing the resource modelling and metallurgical test work with Synectiq Inc., as announced on May 7, 2026. The test work is designed to characterize the principal ore types, evaluate copper, molybdenum, and silver recoveries, and assess concentrate quality. The results are intended to support assumptions for an updated mineral resource estimate and future technical studies.

About Flor de Cobre

Flor de Cobre is located 35 kilometres southeast of Arequipa and straddles the border between the Departments of Arequipa and Moquegua, the Provinces of Arequipa and General Sanchez Cerro, and the Districts of Polobaya and La Capilla.

The property is comprised of eleven mining concessions for a total of 2,984.4 hectares ("ha") which are 100% owned by the Company's Peruvian subsidiary Candelaria Resources S.A.C. The project is in the Southern Perú Copper Belt, which is host to numerous porphyry Cu-Mo deposits, including the Cerro Verde Cu-Mo mine operated by Freeport-McMoRan2; the Cuajone and Toquepala Cu-Mo mines operated by Southern Copper2; and the Quellaveco Cu-Mo mine operated by Anglo American2. Flor de Cobre is 5 kilometres northwest of the Chapi Mine and 26 kilometres southeast of the Cerro Verde Mine (Figure 1).

Flor de Cobre hosts the Atravesado porphyry Cu-Mo target, a classic Andean porphyry system with Cu-Mo mineralization potentially associated with a multi-phase quartz monzonite porphyry complex. Atravesado is characterized by widespread Cu-oxide mineralization and strong surface rock Cu geochemistry associated with lower Cretaceous-aged quartzite and sandstone sedimentary rocks which form the upper part of the Yura Group. These rocks are also cut by several narrow potassic altered quartz monzonite porphyry dykes.

The property is situated at a modest elevation of 2,700 metres with excellent infrastructure for future mine development and is accessible along paved and maintained unpaved roads from the hub-city of Arequipa.

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Entrée Resources Ltd. (TSX:ETG; OTCQB:ERLFF – the “Company” or “Entrée”) is pleased to provide an update on its recent engagement with the Government Working Group in Mongolia. Additionally, the Company is pleased to provide analytical results received from the Company’s joint venture partner Oyu Tolgoi LLC (“OT LLC”) for an additional seven underground infill diamond drill holes (“DDH”) at the Hugo North Extension (“HNE”) deposit on the Entrée/Oyu Tolgoi joint venture property (the “Entrée/Oyu Tolgoi JV Property”) in Mongolia. The drill holes were completed by OT LLC between 2023 and 2026 (see Table 1 below).  

ENGAGEMENT WITH GOVERNMENT WORKING GROUP
On November 9 and 10, 2026, the Company met with members of the Government Working Group in Mongolia to commence negotiations for the purpose of resolving outstanding matters in relation to the Shivee Tolgoi and Javkhlant mining licenses (the “Licenses”). The newly reconstituted Government Working Group was established on October 2, 2026 pursuant to Order No.217 of the Prime Minister of Mongolia and is led by the Minister of Justice and Internal Affairs. At the meeting, the parties agreed a framework for negotiations comprising four key points:

  • The parties shall make reasonable efforts to resolve the outstanding matters in accordance with the Constitution of Mongolia, applicable laws, and the applicable legal framework within the first quarter 2027. Should the parties be unable to reach an agreement within such period, the parties may mutually agree on an extension of the negotiation period.
  • The parties expressly acknowledge that, pursuant to Article 8.1.7 of the Minerals Law of Mongolia, the Parliament of Mongolia has the authority to determine the State’s shareholding percentage in the private legal entity holding the Shivee Tolgoi and Javkhlant mining licenses of strategic importance, and to decide whether such shareholding is to be replaced by a special royalty for the use of mineral resources of a mineral deposit, noting that nothing herein prejudges the form, scope or structure of any such arrangement, which remains subject to negotiation and all necessary approvals and consents.
  • Any transfer of the Licenses shall be undertaken in accordance with applicable law and all required approvals.
  • The parties shall make reasonable efforts to ensure that the composition of their authorized working group remains unchanged for the duration of the negotiations.

The Company’s next step is to prepare, in consultation with other stakeholders, a revised proposal for consideration by the Government Working Group. The Company’s principal corporate objectives continue to be resolution of State participation in the area of the Licenses and transfer of the Licenses to OT LLC in accordance with applicable laws and the Company’s contracts. The Company remains committed to working towards a constructive solution that serves the interests of all Oyu Tolgoi project stakeholders and enables OT LLC to resume Lift 1 underground development and extraction activities on the Shivee Tolgoi license area.

  • UGD918A: 67.6 metres grading 1.07% CuEq.

HNE DRILLING RESULTS

The additional DDH analytical results received from OT LLC are from underground infill diamond drilling programs undertaken between 2023 and 2026 on the HNE deposit.  These underground DDHs were all collared from existing infrastructure on the Oyu Tolgoi mining licence (100% OT LLC) and drilled towards the northwest or northeast onto the Entrée/Oyu Tolgoi JV Property.  The DDHs targeted mineralization within the existing footprint of the HNE deposit in the proposed Lift 2 block cave or were drilled for geotechnical purposes in areas surrounding the mineralization (Figure 1).  Details about several of the newly reported drill holes, including DDH locations, were previously disclosed by Entrée on July 18, 2024 (see the news release titled, “Entrée Resources Announces Additional Drill Results And Provides An Update On Underground Development Work”), on February 27, 2025 (see the news release titled, “Entrée Announces Drill Results From Hugo North Extension and Heruga Deposits”), and on April 9, 2026 (see the news released titled, “Entrée Resources Provides JV Licenses Update and Drill and Regional Exploration Results”).

DDH UGD757A was drilled at a moderate dip towards the northeast, parallel to the trend of the porphyry deposit.  After crossing onto the Entrée/Oyu Tolgoi JV Property the DDH entered moderate grade copper mineralization and low-grade gold mineralization hosted in quartz monzodiorite for the duration of the drill hole.  

DDH UGD918 (and daughter hole UGD918A) was collared on the Oyu Tolgoi mining licence and drilled at a moderate dip towards the northeast.  After crossing onto the Entrée/Oyu Tolgoi JV Property it immediately entered the central portion of the HNE deposit and was drilled parallel to the main mineralized trend in moderately phyllic altered, quartz monzodiorite, cut by occasional basalt andesite dikes.  The quartz monzodiorite is mineralized with 3-5% sulphides with mostly chalcopyrite and lesser bornite, along with minor pyrite and returned moderate to high grades of copper and gold as shown in Table 1.  The DDH terminated in strong mineralization. 

DDH UGD1012A was collared on the Oyu Tolgoi mining licence and drilled at a moderate dip towards the northeast. Once crossing onto the Entrée/Oyu Tolgoi JV Property the DDH entered moderately copper and gold mineralized quartz monzodiorite porphyry but was terminated 10.5 metres after crossing the boundary.

Underground DDH UGD1016 was collared on the Oyu Tolgoi mining licence and drilled at a moderate dip towards the north. Once crossing onto the Entrée/Oyu Tolgoi JV Property the DDH entered 60 meters of unmineralized footwall biotite granodiorite to the west of the main HNE deposit. No significant grades of copper or gold were returned from this drill hole.

Underground DDH UGD1025A was drilled from the Oyu Tolgoi mining licence to the northwest at a moderate to steep dip.  After crossing onto the Entrée/Oyu Tolgoi JV Property the DDH entered into phyllic altered quartz monzodiorite, with minor intervals of biotite granodiorite and basalt andesite dikes, which changed to potassic alteration further down the hole.  Copper and gold grades remained strong until about 488 metres depth, beyond which the DDH crossed out of the western edge of the HNE deposit and grades were weakly anomalous until the end of the hole.

The final underground drill hole with analytical results is UGD1053, which was collared from an underground drill pad on the Oyu Tolgoi mining licence, east of the HNE deposit. The drill hole was drilled northeast at a moderate dip, remaining parallel to, and just east of the edge of the HNE deposit and was designed primarily for geotechnical purposes.  The drill hole crossed a mix of advanced argillic and phyllic altered porphyritic augite basalt and ignimbrite with several basalt andesite dikes. Copper grades remained low grade over most of the drill holes while gold grades were anomalous to low grade.

2026 HNE and Regional Drill Hole Information

Collars for the 2026 HNE underground drill holes were surveyed using a Leica TS16 instrument and downhole surveys were collected approximately every 30 metres using an IMDEX EZ-TrackTM driller operated, multi-shot survey instrument. Collars for the HNE surface and regional drill holes were surveyed using either an Emlid Reach RS3 or Trimble GPS R10 GPS system and downhole surveys were collected approximately every 30 metres using an EZ-TRAC digital instrument.  The 2026 HNE surface and regional drill holes were collared with PQ diameter core (123 mm) and often reduced to HQ (96 mm) core diameter at depth.  Underground holes at HNE were collared using HQ diameter and occasionally reduced to NQ (76 mm) at depth. 

Drill core from the 14 underground DDHs and two surface DDHs reported for HNE and for the three regional exploration DDHs and eight condemnation DDHs were geologically and geotechnically logged at site by OT LLC.  All core was saw-cut on site before being bagged and shipped to the laboratory.  Samples were either quarter core or half core depending on whether a portion was also used for metallurgical test work or other purposes.  Sample lengths generally averaged approximately 2.0 metres and core recovery was recorded as being very good (>95% recovery), except in localized areas of faulting/fracturing. 

Core from 2026 HNE drilling was shipped to ALS Laboratory (“ALS”) in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, for sample preparation.  ALS is independent of OT LLC, Rio Tinto and Entrée. At ALS the samples were crushed to <2mm and pulverized to 75μm, then the pulps were shipped directly by ALS to their laboratory in Perth, Australia for analysis. HNE samples were predominantly analyzed for gold by ICP21 (30g fire assay with ICP-AES finish) and a multi-element package including copper, silver and molybdenum by MS61 (four-acid digestion of 0.25g sample paired with ICP-MS). Copper values greater than approximately 1.0% were further analyzed by OG62 (ore grade copper using a 0.4 g sample and a 4-acid digestion with an ICP finish).

Core from regional exploration drilling were shipped to ALS Laboratory in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia for sample preparation. At ALS, the samples were crushed to <2mm and pulverized to 75μm, then the pulps were shipped directly by ALS to their laboratory in Perth, Australia for analysis. Samples were predominantly analyzed for gold by ICP21 (30g fire assay with ICP-AES finish) and a 48-element package including copper, silver and molybdenum by MS61L (four-acid digestion of 0.25 g sample paired with ICP-MS).   

Core from condemnation drillholes were shipped to SGS Laboratory in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia for sample preparation and analysis. SGS is independent of OT LLC, Rio Tinto and Entrée.  At SGS the samples were crushed to <2mm and pulverized to 75μm.  Samples were predominantly analyzed for gold by fire assay (30g FA with AAS finish) and a multi-element package including copper, silver and molybdenum by IC40M (ICP-MS after four-acid digestion).

OT LLC follows a rigorous quality assurance/quality control (“QAQC”) program for the sampling programs that includes the regular insertion of standards, blanks and duplicates into the sample stream. The QP is not aware of any drilling, sampling, recovery, or other factors that could materially affect the accuracy or reliability of the data referred to in this disclosure.

QUALIFIED PERSON
